visual.title: One equation, several curves
visual.caption: The general equation Ax² + Bxy + Cy² + Dx + Ey + F = 0 covers every conic. A and C set the quadratic shape before rotation, and B turns the axes. When A and C have the same sign, raising |B| past 2√(AC) changes the sign of B² − 4AC, so an ellipse becomes a hyperbola; exactly at the boundary the curve is a pair of parallel lines. A linear term D or E is what makes a parabola possible.

predict.question: With A = 1 and C = 0.5, raise the cross term B from 0. What happens when B passes √2?
predict.explain: B rotates the principal axes. The discriminant B² − 4AC changes sign at B = 2√(AC) = √2. Below it the curve is an ellipse, above it a hyperbola, and exactly at it the curve is two parallel lines. A parabola needs a linear term.
